rationale: The assistant immediately recognised an RCD trip as an earth-leakage fault, told the customer to stop resetting, leave it unplugged and get an engineer to insulation-test the heater, pumps and wiring, which matches the ground truth's safety boundary and sensible first step almost exactly. It hedged appropriately ('most often points to'), named the heater as likely without asserting certainty, and limited the customer to safe visual checks of plug/cable and floor water with the appliance isolated and panels left on. Minor weaknesses: it did not acknowledge the model number, did not directly ask whether only hot programmes trip or whether trips occur with the dishwasher unplugged (the electrician discriminator), and oddly flagged 'the point in the cycle' as helpful when the customer had already given it. Overall a homeowner would be well served and safely escalated.
